**Task complete.** Both tests pass.

The bug was a mutable default argument. Using `bucket=[]` creates one list object when the function is defined, and every call without an explicit bucket shares that list. The fix uses `bucket=None` (immutable) and creates a fresh list only when needed. This is a Python footgun that trips up even experienced developersâ€”always use `None` as the default for mutable arguments.
